title: Visible identity browser
summary: yoke browser open --project P --identity NAME URL shows a URL in a visible window of an authorized identity's profile, so the page opens signed in. It uses the same Chromium binary and flags as the sign-in window, plus a loopback DevTools port. When a browser already runs on that profile, the URL opens as a new tab there; a QA daemon on that profile is stopped first. The command reads only the machine-local profile and needs no control-plane connection. An identity never authorized refuses browser_identity_not_authorized and names yoke browser authorize --project P --identity NAME --test-machine TEST_MACHINE. On test machines it is the standard BROWSER opener for installer approvals and the desktop link handler on Linux and WSL. Exploratory missions without named identities open each page with it for the project's default_identity, never the stock desktop browser. On native Windows, yoke browser open and the managed yoke qa browser commands sent through the mission host command start in the test user's interactive desktop through a scheduled-task handoff, with the installed Yoke's Python, because an SSH session shows no window. The internal yoke browser devtools tabs|approve, owned by yoke_harness.identity_browser_devtools, is how the approval driver reads those DevTools ports through the machine's installed Yoke over SSH. Live host proof is still owed.
